summary: When the project has an approved Process Policy, `delivery_compile.py approve-scope` pins its path, revision and source hash in `delivery.md`, inside the scope hash, so each Delivery names the process switch values it ran under; a draft or invalid policy refuses scope approval. Without a policy nothing is pinned and every Delivery compiler output stays byte-identical, which a golden all-default run now proves, and the Delivery runs with every switch at its default. The pin is compared by value while an execution approval can still re-pin it: for a scope- or execution-approved Delivery, an approved policy that changes the value of a switch a Delivery flow owns makes `check` and the coordinator verbs that run it refuse the Delivery, naming each changed switch and the plan revision that pins the new values, in order, until `approve-execution` re-pins the current policy and lists the changed fields in `refreshed_delivery_pins`; a policy that changes none of those values, one with every switch at its default included, agrees with a Delivery that pinned none. `process_policy.py value --delivery DLV-###` and `delivery_compile.py`'s own switch reads refuse such a change of the switch they read instead of reading the new value. From the Delivery Review on, and for a merged or cancelled Delivery, the pin is kept as the record of what the Delivery ran under and its revision's values are read back, from the current policy or from Git history by the pinned source hash, so a policy set for the next Delivery never changes them; `value` then reports the commit that held the revision. Setup's project refresh declares the new `delivery.md` properties in `.obsidian/types.json`.
